teaser.text: AbbVie is a prescription-drug company: it turns scientific discoveries into treatments, sells them through doctors, payers and distributors, and keeps what remains after discounts and costs. Its business is easiest to understand by following the medicines, the money paid for them, and the factories and partnerships that make the sales possible.

blocks.heading: What has to go right, and what could go wrong for AbbVie?

paragraphs.text: The bear case holds first-year revenue at $73,000 million, then reduces it to $72,500 million and $72,000 million. Its margins fall from 39.9% to 37.0% because older-product erosion, payer pressure and Apogee costs offset replacement growth. The bull case reaches $75,000 million of revenue initially and then $84,000 million and $94,000 million, with margins reaching 43.0%. That requires growth above management’s high-single-digit description.

The base is supported by Skyrizi and Rinvoq, which supplied 42.3% of 2025 revenue. Each grew about 24% in the latest quarter, while neuroscience also grew strongly. The risk is concentration: Humira declined 35.9% in that quarter, and Apogee is expected to reduce adjusted EPS before contributing earnings.

blocks.heading: How much cash does AbbVie really make?

paragraphs.text: Stock-based pay deserves a separate deduction. AbbVie granted $955 million of stock compensation in 2025. The cash-flow statement adds it back because no cash was paid, but employees received part of the ownership of the business. After that analytical deduction, free cash flow per diluted share fell 0.4%.

blocks.heading: How much does AbbVie pay in dividends per share?

paragraphs.text: The dividend base case rises from $7.19 to $7.91 per share as quarterly payments increase. The bear case holds the annual amount at $6.92, despite AbbVie’s long record of increases. The bull case reaches $8.34 because stronger cash generation permits larger raises, while acquisition spending and debt make that outcome less likely.

blocks.heading: Does AbbVie’s cash cover its dividend?

paragraphs.text: The company’s operating medicines generated substantial free cash flow. The calculation used here subtracts stock compensation, because shares given to employees dilute existing owners even though they do not require an immediate cash payment. AbbVie recorded $955 million of stock-based compensation in 2025 and received $172 million when employees exercised options.

Dividends and acquisitions narrow the remaining choice further. AbbVie paid $11,657 million in dividends in 2025, while external acquisitions and investments also used cash. The cash engine is powerful, but conventional free cash flow is not the same as cash available to reduce debt or buy the next medicine.

blocks.heading: What has AbbVie guided for the year?

paragraphs.text: AbbVie’s weighted path reaches $283.21 by October 2027 and $313.79 by October 2029, a 23% return including dividends by the final date; it hinges on replacement-franchise growth, earnings conversion and the valuation multiple. Management guides to 2026 adjusted diluted EPS of $13.76–$13.96 and $1,251 million of acquired research and milestone expense, while targeting $31,000 million of combined SKYRIZI and RINVOQ revenue in 2027. The probability-weighted cases are bear, base and bull.

blocks.heading: Has AbbVie kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: The annual bonus focuses on the business replacing Humira, AbbVie’s older blockbuster medicine. “Platform Revenue” means sales excluding Humira, adjusted for currency. It reached $56.3 billion against a $53.7 billion target in 2025. That measure asks whether management is building the next engine of the company rather than receiving credit for sales that were expected to fade.

The promise showed progress. AbbVie’s 2025 revenue reached $61.160 billion, up 8.6%. Adjusted earnings per share, however, fell 1.2% to $10.00, partly reflecting the cost of acquired research and milestones. “Adjusted” figures can help compare operations, but excluded costs still matter to shareholders.

blocks.heading: What has AbbVie reported in recent results?
What should I watch in AbbVie results?

paragraphs.text: The first checkpoint is October 30, when the company reports its third-quarter results. This is the first report containing Apogee after its September closing. Investors should examine medicine demand, the effect of disclosed deal charges, and the change in cash and debt—not just the EPS headline.

Apogee’s lead program was expected to begin major eczema trials in the second half of 2026, with maintenance results following in 2027. Other pipeline milestones cover skin disease, lupus, blood cancers and eye disease. A planned readout provides information; it does not guarantee approval.
